Service Requirements The Contractor must provide printing services, including the following tasks: • Graphic design and creation of annual report content for various Embassy offices. • Graphic design and creation of brochures, information portfolios, folders, advertising publications, flyers, and similar materials for the Embassy's promotional events. • Printing and/or photocopying of documents, brochures, and portfolios in a professional manner, ensuring clear colors, photographs, text, and images for finished products. Preference will be given to contractors offering multiple printing methods, such as commercial, digital, press, and web-based printing. • Supplying stock images for publications, as needed. • Providing printing designs for requesting offices to review and confirm prior to production. The Contractor is responsible for installing, setting up, and delivering printed items to U.S. Embassy Hanoi events. • Material Requirements: The Contractor shall present several material options for the Embassy's selection prior to submitting a quote. Services must include all necessary supplies — such as equipment, toner, developer, fuser agent, staples, paper, g

Lisboa sob o Nº 508 481 287 Contribuinte Nº 508 481 287 3 SERVIÇO DE GESTÃO DE COMPRAS Obrigações do prestador de serviços Subsecção I Disposições gerais Cláusula 4.ª Obrigações principais do prestador de serviços 1. Sem prejuízo de outras obrigações previstas na legislação aplicável, no Caderno de Encargos ou nas cláusulas contratuais, da celebração do contrato decorrem para o prestador de serviços as seguintes obrigações principais: a) Obrigação de prestar os serviços identificados na proposta e melhor descritos no Anexo I ao presente Caderno de Encargos; b) Afetar à prestação de serviço, e as expensas suas, todos os componentes, materiais, equipamentos e ferramentas necessárias; c) Afetar à prestação de serviços toda a mão-de-obra qualificada necessária, sem encargos acrescidos para o ULSSM; d) Cumprir o disposto no artigo 419º-A do CCP; e) Obrigação de garantir o disposto nos números 3 e 4 da

rte utilizado. 7. Para efeitos da execução e ao abrigo do contrato, o ULSSM e o prestador de serviços procedem às seguintes atividades de tratamento de dados pessoais: a) O prestador de serviços trata dados pessoais de representantes, trabalhadores e/ou utentes do ULSSM; b) O ULSSM trata dados pessoais de representantes, trabalhadores, agentes, subcontratados e consultores do prestador de serviços. 2. O tratamento dos dados pessoais encontra-se limitado, nos termos do artigo 6.º, n.º 1, alíneas b) e c) do RGPD, a finalidades exclusivamente relacionadas com a execução da prestação de serviços ou com o cumprimento de obrigações jurídicas a que o ULSSM e o prestador de serviços estejam adstritos. 3. O ULSSM e o prestador de serviços assumem a obrigação de estrita confidencialidade relativamente a todos os dados pessoais de que venham a ter conhecimento no âmbito do contrato, extensiva à informação a que os seus trabalhadores, agentes, subcontratados e consultores tenham acesso, garantindo que os mesmos assumiram um compromisso de confidencialidade. 4. O ULSSM e o prestador de serviços apenas podem transmitir dados pessoais a que tenham acess

Over the past decade, this ecosystem has expanded organically through project ‑by‑project deployments. As a result, the current environment is characterised by fragmentation, inconsistent branding, duplication of operational and hosting costs, varied technical standards, and increasingly complex governance and content‑management structures. A preliminary mapping exercise conducted by MTA has identified more than thirty (30) digital assets, including consumer‑facing websites, corporate platforms, country‑specific domains (e.g., 14 Unclassified France, Germany, Italy, the UK, Japan, Korea, and others), MICE ‑focused portals, event ‑driven microsites, and international representative sites. These range from high ‑traffic multilingual portals such as VisitMalta.com to legacy campaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal syst

mpaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal systems supporting media management, CRM, B2B services, and training. Social media channels and API ‑based integrations further contribute to the broader content flow and technical landscape. MTA’s strategic direction is to consolidate this extensive and heterogeneous digital landscape under a unified and coherent platform centred around VisitMalta.com. The objective is to improve user experience, reinforce consistent brand representation across all markets, streamline content and technical governance, and reduce long‑term operational, maintenance, and hosting costs. To support this strategic shift, MTA requires a comprehensive Web Environment Analysis and Requirements Definition Exercise. It shall assess the current ecosystem in full, map underlying systems and content flows, identify consolidation and rationalisation opportunities, and define the technical, functional, governance, integration, and procurement requirements. The findings will directly inform the preparation of a public tender, ensuring that the future solution is robust, scalable, interoperable, secure, and aligned with MTA’s long‑term digital transformation strategy. 1.6 - Related Programmes and Donor Activities T

To carry out a complete and validated analysis of MTA’s current digital ecosystem This objective focuses on discovering, mapping, auditing, and assessing all MTA digital assets, including domains, subdomains, microsites, hosting environments, CMS platforms, integrations, 15 Unclassified SEO structures, and compliance obligations. The Consultant shall categorise each asset using a Retain / Migrate / Redesign / Retire model. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote orpre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boo

tact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommended standard Army

ughput: Batch processing at MEPS and IET Reception facilities. o Remote Self-Assessment: A mobile self-service assessment accessible via standard smart devices for geographically dispersed individuals. This includes pre-accession Cadets and in-service Soldiers requiring sizing for pre-deployment, unit-level equipment fielding, or periodic data updates in both garrison and austere field environments. • Usability: Must be highly intuitive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. The scope covers four primary initial accession pipelines: (1) Initial Entry Training (IET) Soldiers processing through Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS); (2) United States Military Academy (West Point) Cadets; (3) contracted Senior Reserve Officers' Training Co

A critical capability gap exists for a scalable, consistent, and data-driven method to capture Soldier and Cadet body and foot measurements and seamlessly translate them into accurate uniform and footwear sizing recommendations. Uniform and footwear sizing for Army Soldiers at accession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. ns. Uniform and footwear sizing for Army Soldiers at accession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote orpre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initia

elding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boots, downstream exchanges, and an inconsistent experience across different geographic locations. At the tactical and operational levels, these sizing inaccuracies lead to excess inventory of mis-forecasted sizes and highly inefficient supply chain management. To address these challenges, the Army is seeking a commercial solution capable of accurately capturing both body and foot measurements using automated, digital, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. The Contractor shall deliver fully operational, integrated, and sustained EW SITE systems and sub-system components for domestic and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. The required outcome is an EW SITE system capable of supporting a multitude of laboratory-specific System Configurations across multiple platforms (EA-18G, F/A-18, MH-60) while maintaining configuration consistency with the Advanced Weapons Laboratory (AWL) at NAWCWD China Lake, CA. Additionally, the Contractor shall ensure continuous operational readiness of current EW SITE systems through comprehensive lifecycle support, including on-call and on-site maintenance, system upgrades, replacement parts provisioning, and personnel training. When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. Isikuandmete töötlemine Lepingu täitmisega seotud isikuandmete töötlemisel tuleb rakendada asjakohaseid tehnilisi ja korralduslikke meetmeid sellisel viisil, et töötlemine vastab isikuandmete kaitse üldmääruses (GDPR) ja isikuandmete kaitse seaduses sätestatud nõuetele (edaspidi koos: Isikuandmete õigusaktid). See kõrvalejätmise alus hõlmab ka korruptsiooni avaliku sektori hankija (võrgustiku sektori hankija) või ettevõtja riigi õiguses sätestatud määratluses.</cbc:Description> <cac:Legislation> <cbc:ID schemeID="CriteriaTaxonomy" schemeAgencyID="EU-COM-GROW" schemeVersionID="2.0.2">c753a2c5-59e6-4970-b6eb-27224e96bf76</cbc:ID> <cbc:Title languageID="ET">RHS § 95 lg 1 p 1 ja lg 2 "keda või kelle haldus-, juhtimis- või järelevalveorgani liiget, prokuristi või muud isikut, kellel on volitus seda ettevõtjat esindada, tema nimel otsuseid teha või teda kontrollida, on karistatud aususe kohustuse rikkumise või korruptiivse teo eest". Kui hankemenetlusest kõrvaldamise alus esineb, võib ettevõtja soovi korral esitada tõendeid selle kohta, et ta on võtnud meetmeid oma usaldusväärsuse taastamiseks. Heastamise võim
